'''The [[1987 in association football|1987]]–[[1988 in association football|88]] season''' was the 89th completed season of [[The Football League]].

==Final league tables and results ==

The tables and results below are reproduced here in the exact form that they can be found at [https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1987-88.html The Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation] website,<ref name="rsssf">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1987-88.html |title=England 1987–88 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=2010-02-24| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100127122453/http://www.rsssf.com/engpaul/FLA/1987-88.html| archive-date= 27 January 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> with home and away statistics separated.

[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] won the league title by nine points, and with only two defeats all season. Second in the league were [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].

The automatically relegated sides were [[Watford F.C.|Watford]], [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] and [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]]. [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] were subsequently relegated as well after losing to [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] in the playoff final.

[[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] lifted the [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]] championship trophy and gained promotion to the First Division for the first time in their history. Runners-up were [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], and [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] won promotion via [[play-offs]].

[[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] and [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] were relegated.

===Second Division play-offs===
The team fourth from bottom of the First Division played off for one place in that division with the teams finishing third, fourth and fifth in the Second Division. In the semi-final, [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] of the First Division beat fifth-placed [[Blackburn Rovers]] 6–1 on aggregate, and third-placed [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] beat [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]] 3–2 on aggregate. The final was also played [[two-legged tie|over two legs]]. Playing at their [[Ayresome Park]] ground in front of a crowd of 25,531, Middlesbrough duly won the first leg 2–0 with goals from [[Bernie Slaven]] and [[Trevor Senior]]. In the second leg at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]], which was marred by violence perpetrated by some of the 40,550 spectators, Chelsea's [[Gordon Durie]] scored the only goal. Thus Middlesbrough won 2–1 on aggregate and were promoted to the [[1988–89 Football League#First Division|First Division for 1988–89]], while Chelsea were relegated to the Second.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rsssf.com/engpaul/fla/1987-88.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010502035637/http://www.rsssf.com/engpaul/FLA/1987-88.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 May 2001 |title=Season 1987–88 |first=Paul |last=Felton |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation (RSSSF) |access-date=26 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bounder.friardale.co.uk/Results/1987.htm |title=Chelsea Football Club Match Results Season 1987–1988 |website=bounder.friardale.co.uk |access-date=26 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.gazettelive.co.uk/news/teesside-news/the-battle-stamford-bridge-violent-9783533 |title='The Battle of Stamford Bridge': Violent scenes on a victorious day for Boro |first=Sophie |last=Barley |newspaper=The Gazette |location=Middlesbrough |date=3 August 2015 |access-date=26 May 2016}}</ref>

[[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] won the [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]] and went back up to the [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]]. They were joined by runners-up [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] and playoff winners [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]]. The automatic relegation places were occupied by [[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]], [[York City F.C.|York City]] and [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]], with [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] relegated after play-offs.<ref name=eflt>{{cite web |last1=Edward Ackers |title=Season 1987-88 |url=http://www.englishfootballleaguetables.co.uk/final/f1987-88.html |website=English Football League Tables |access-date=6 August 2019}}</ref>

==[[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]]==

Wolves ended their two-year tenure in the [[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]] by finishing top of the table and winning promotion to the [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]]. They also won the [[Football League Trophy|Sherpa Van Trophy]] [[1988 Football League Trophy Final|final]] by defeating [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] at Wembley.

[[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]], [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] and [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] were also promoted.

[[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]] were relegated for the second successive season. They were replaced in the Football League by [[Lincoln City F.C.|Lincoln City]].
